summary_html: A **judge orders** CPS to investigate or assess during civil/criminal proceedings. Federal funding statutes (ASFA/IV-E) tether court findings to child-welfare actions, embedding judicial oversight into intake-to-case flow.

key_cases.case_name: Tyner v. Department of Social & Health Services, Child Protective Services
key_cases.holding: The court held that RCW 26.44.050 impliedly creates a negligent-investigation cause of action in favor of a child's parents, including parents themselves suspected of abuse, and that a later judicial no-contact order does not automatically break legal causation unless all material information was placed before the court.
key_cases.relevance: Holds that the agency's statutory investigative duty exists independently of any court involvement, so a judicially generated referral does not displace the agency's own duty of care.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that under RCW 26.44.050, CPS owes a duty of care to a child's parents, even those suspected of abusing their own children, when investigating allegations of child abuse.

key_cases.holding: The court held that DSHS caseworkers have no absolute immunity for foster placement decisions made outside an adversarial judicial process, that they may claim only the Guffey qualified immunity, which requires carrying out a statutory duty by statutory procedures and acting reasonably, and that the State itself has no immunity from suit.
key_cases.relevance: Holds that a court order procured ex parte and without any adversarial evaluation of the placement does not confer absolute immunity on the caseworkers who obtained it.
key_cases.quote: Caseworkers cannot claim even a qualified immunity when they fail to follow statutory procedures.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed summary judgment for DSHS, holding that a dependency court's order is a superseding intervening cause cutting off caseworker liability for negligent investigation unless the faulty investigation deprived that court of material information, and that Petcu identified no material information withheld from the dependency judge.
key_cases.relevance: Defines when judicial involvement in a case breaks the causal chain between the agency's own investigation and the resulting separation of parent and child.
key_cases.quote: Otherwise, court intervention operates as a superseding intervening cause that cuts off the caseworker's liability.
